creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: The caption figure of $11 billion quarterly revenue, up 378%, looks garbled or misstated relative to SanDisk's usual scale; it is reported here as captioned.
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA examines SanDisk's crash — down over 22% in a day and 53% in a month — after a US midterm election result that handed Democrats control of the House and Senate and saw several anti-data-centre referendums pass. The market fears slower data-centre construction and therefore slower orders for SanDisk's products, despite strong results a week earlier: the captions state revenue of $11 billion, up 378% year over year, with $5.7 billion of operating cash flow, a CFO-to-sales ratio above 50%. He argues the sell-off prices in the worst case — that data centres are never built — before the newly elected legislators have even formed a plan, and that building could simply stretch over more years or move to friendlier states. SanDisk was already cheap and is now, in his view, ridiculously undervalued at a forward P/E of 2.8. His model has free cash flow rising from $8 billion in 2026 to $31 billion in 2027 and $38 billion in 2028, then growing very slowly on replacement demand and higher prices, giving a fair value of $1,808 against a current price of $806. Call: SNDK BUY reiterated, conviction upgraded from low to medium. He also notes Nvidia's 17 November earnings as the next catalyst.
title: Why Is Sandisk Stock Crashing, and is it a Generational Buying Opportunity? | SNDK Stock Analysis

calls.price_at_call: FV $1,808 vs current ~$806 after a 22% one-day drop; forward P/E 2.8
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated, conviction upgraded low to medium: the post-election AI sell-off prices in a worst case (data centers never built) that has not happened; an already-cheap stock is now 'ridiculously undervalued' on his FCF model.
calls.base_case: FCF booms in FY27-28 ($31B rising to $38B) then moderates to slow replacement-driven growth; FV $1,808.
calls.bull_case: Data-center build-out continues, just spread over more years or in other states; replacement demand plus higher prices sustain growth.
calls.bear_case: Democratic House/Senate and local anti-data-center measures slow the build-out materially; the memory boom peaks and FCF stalls.
